chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man said, 'If I die, my slave is free,' and the man has a debt. He said: 'If he dies while having a debt that covers the price of the slave, the slave is sold; and if it does not cover the price of the slave, the slave is asked to work (to seek ease) in paying the debt of his master, and he is free when he pays it off.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave if the owner dies with debt?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the priority of debt repayment over the execution of a will for manumission, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that creditors' rights supersede the testator's discretionary gifts. It establishes a nuanced legal mechanism where the slave’s value is assessed against the debt, ensuring fair settlement either through sale or continued service until emancipation. This ruling underscores the balance between fulfilling religious obligations of freeing slaves and maintaining economic justice for creditors.
